fields.meta_description: Build a tenant satisfaction survey from a prompt, with building scores, repair follow-ups, renewal intent, and move-in checks.
fields.h1: Build a Tenant Satisfaction Survey for Every Building
fields.hero_description: Build a tenant satisfaction survey that scores each building, sends low ratings to one manager, and saves answers you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Tenant Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions and the table of answers behind them, and a follow-up prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_1:
Sections drafted from your portfolio

Tell Emergent how many buildings you manage and what residents should rate, like repairs and noise. It drafts a section per topic, and you edit any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer tagged with building and unit

Each response saves as a row in a database you own, with building, unit, and survey round attached. Put last spring's repair score beside this spring's in one table.
fields.feature_3:
Low scores reach the person who can act

Set a floor, such as a building average under 3.0, and the app sends that building's manager an email or Slack message with the comments. Buildings above it stay in the report.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Residents tap through one question per screen from an email link or a mailroom flyer. Emergent sets no cap on responses, for a 40-unit walk-up or a 4,000-unit portfolio.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders that stop once a unit answers

Units that have not answered get an email reminder before the survey closes. Once a resident submits, reminders to that unit stop, and the dashboard shows who is still out.
fields.feature_6:
A survey link on your own domain

Residents open the survey at an address on your own domain, which Emergent includes and which uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Property Teams Act on Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
One building under 3.0 goes to the regional manager

Calloway Property Group surveys all 412 units each spring, and any building averaging under 3.0 on maintenance response goes to the regional manager. This year, Linden Court averaged 2.6 out of 5 from 58 answers, while every other building scored 3.9 or higher. Teodora Vance got its scores and comments that day.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a resident says the leak is not fixed, the job reopens

When a work order closes at Ferrow Apartments, the resident gets 2 questions: was the problem fixed, and how did the visit go. The resident in unit 4B answered No about a kitchen faucet leak. The app reopened the work order for Gus Pelham, the maintenance supervisor, due within 48 hours, comment attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seven residents unlikely to renew, all on one list

Sable Ridge Apartments asks residents how likely they are to renew, on a 1 to 5 scale, 90 days before the lease ends. Of 38 leases ending in March, 29 residents answered, and 7 chose 1 or 2. Those 7 units went on one list for Corinne Abate, the leasing manager, and 4 of the 7 named parking as the reason.
fields.tab_content_4:
Clean at move-in for only 13 of 21 new residents

Orchard Mill Lofts sends new residents a yes-or-no survey 14 days after move-in, and 21 answered last quarter. Working keys drew a yes from 20 of 21 and smoke alarms from 21 of 21, but only 13 of 21 said the unit was clean when they arrived. The turnover crew added a deep-clean step to the make-ready checklist.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Tenant Satisfaction Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a tenant satisfaction survey that residents finish and that ends in fixes they can see.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the decision the answers feed
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what the results will change before you draft a question: next year's repair budget or the landscaping contract. Cut any question that feeds none of them. Put the decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the survey around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Split "How satisfied are you with maintenance and communication?" into two questions. Pew Research Center says double-barreled questions are difficult for respondents to answer. One topic per question also tells you which part of the service to fix.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Rate repairs and parking on their own before asking how satisfied a resident is overall. Pew Research Center has found that the order in which questions are asked can influence how people respond. Keep the order the same every round.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the same 5-point satisfaction scale on every rating question and in every building. A 3.2 at one property then means the same as a 3.2 at another, and this spring's score lines up against last spring's without any conversion.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Before the link goes out, have 5 residents from different buildings answer it. Pew calls pretesting an essential step in questionnaire design. Rewrite any question two of them read differently, and check that each answer saved with the right unit.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it from a name residents know
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email the link from the property manager's address and post a printed copy in the mailroom. Keep the survey open for 2 weeks, and send one reminder after the first week to units that have not answered yet.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing, post each building's scores and the 2 or 3 fixes you picked, with a date for each. Ask the same questions next round, and the scores show whether the fixes moved anything.

faq_plan.q: What is a tenant satisfaction survey?
faq_plan.a: A tenant satisfaction survey is a questionnaire a landlord or property manager sends residents to rate living there: repairs, communication, safety, and value for the rent. The scores show what to fix first. Federal offices have their own version: each year, employees in federally owned and leased buildings provide feedback on their physical space via the Tenant Satisfaction Survey.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a tenant satisfaction survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe your buildings, the topics residents should rate, and who should see low scores, and Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the survey and the database behind it. Change any question with a follow-up prompt, then send residents the link. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Is a resident satisfaction survey the same as a tenant satisfaction survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in practice: both ask the people living in a property how well it is run. "Tenant" names the person on the lease, while a resident satisfaction survey also reaches people who live there without signing one, such as family members or residents of a senior living community. Pick one word and use it in every question.

faq_plan.q: Can residents answer a tenant satisfaction survey one question at a time on a phone?
faq_plan.hint: How to use conversational AI for tenant satisfaction surveys?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A conversational survey shows one question per screen, and a resident can finish it on a phone while waiting for the elevator. Emergent builds that flow from a prompt, with no cap on how many residents respond. The same format works for a customer satisfaction survey that a leasing office sends after a tour.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a tenant satisfaction survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask residents to rate what the property team controls: repair speed, whether a repair fixed the problem, staff communication, lighting and safety, noise, and value for the rent. Add one question on renewal plans, and close with one open question on what to fix first. Keep the full survey under 15 questions.

faq_plan.q: How often should I send a tenant satisfaction survey?
faq_plan.a: Run the full survey once a year, in the same month, and this year's scores line up with last year's. Between rounds, ask 2 or 3 questions at moments a resident remembers well, such as the week after a repair or the first month in a new unit. Keep the full survey to its yearly slot and the short ones short.

faq_plan.q: Can a tenant satisfaction survey ask how residents found the property?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add one multiple-choice question on how they first heard about the building, such as a listing site or a friend who lives there. The answers show which channel brings residents who stay. To learn whether renters nearby know the property's name at all, run a brand awareness survey with people who do not live there yet.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up on a low tenant satisfaction survey score?
faq_plan.a: Reply within a week, say what you will change, and give a date. If the survey was confidential, the property manager can call or email that unit directly about its complaint. If it was anonymous, post the fix to the whole building instead, since you cannot tell which unit wrote it. Then check the same question next round to see whether the score moved.

faq_plan.q: Should a tenant satisfaction survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Make it anonymous for candid answers about staff and neighbors, and confidential when you need to fix a problem in one unit. In an anonymous survey, responses are completely separate from any kind of personally identifiable information. In a confidential survey, responses are connected to personal information. On Emergent, either kind saves to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a tenant satisfaction survey follow every maintenance request?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the follow-up is 2 questions at most and arrives within a day of the job closing. An app built on Emergent can connect to your maintenance software through its API and send the survey when each job closes. To follow residents through every stage, from the first tour to move-out, design a customer experience survey instead of adding questions here.

plan.angle: The top 10 is templates (SurveyHero, DoorLoop, SurveySparrow), one property-software vendor (Grace Hill), and government surveys (GSA federal buildings, Army housing, Massachusetts public housing). Each lists questions; none shows what a property team does with an answer. This page shows four tenant surveys built from a prompt, each ending with one person acting: a building score under 3.0 going to the regional manager, a repair a resident says is not fixed reopening its work order, renewal answers of 1 or 2 going to the leasing manager, and a move-in item that fails often enough to change the turnover checklist. The FAQ covers the questions a builder asks: what to ask, how often, anonymity, resident versus tenant wording, and follow-up on low scores.
